findings.description: STRONGEST FINDING. SHEET-MARK-002's text scopes the degrade rule with the word 'positive': "a positive price that rounds to 0 Cents shall be recorded as a degraded anomaly, not a zero mark." Read literally, this qualifier implies non-positive prices (exactly 0.0, or negative) fall outside the stated rule. All three A-runs independently derived exactly that reading: A1 states '0.0 is a legitimate zero mark,' A2 passes 0.0 through to Mark::Value(0) ('a legitimate price of exactly 0.0 is out of the rule's stated scope'), A3 states 'Zero price (price == 0.0) is NOT an anomaly... yields a legitimate Cents(0)' — unanimous, and traced to the spec's own restrictive wording, not an unforced invention. But the real `price_to_cents` does NOT honor this: it degrades on the broader condition `cents <= 0`, so an exact `price_usd = 0.0` and any negative price (e.g. -5.0) are BOTH routed to `Err(DegradeReason::SubCent)`, pinned by the test `zero_and_negative_price_are_degraded_not_a_zero_or_negative_mark` (`price_to_cents(0.0) == Err(SubCent)`, `price_to_cents(-5.0) == Err(SubCent)`). The B-side surfaces the identical gap from the opposite direction: all three B-runs independently reconstruct this exact broader rule as a requirement the code enforces that the given EARS text never states (B1 UB2: 'never Ok(Cents(0)) and never a negative Cents'; B2 point 5: 'covering an exact 0.0 price, any negative price, or a positive price that rounds down to 0'; B3 point 5: same). Both directions land on the same seam: spec text (as literally written) licenses a narrower rule than the code actually implements.

The code further splits degradation into two DISTINCT reason categories the EARS text never mentions at all: `DegradeReason::Permanent` for non-finite input (NaN, +/-Infinity) vs `DegradeReason::SubCent` for non-positive/rounds-to-zero input — pinned by `price_to_cents(f64::NAN) == Err(Permanent)` and `price_to_cents(f64::INFINITY) == Err(Permanent)` vs `price_to_cents(-5.0) == Err(SubCent)`. All three B-runs converge on this exact two-way split. Notably, where the A-side addressed invalid input at all (A2, A3), it grouped negative price together WITH non-finite under one 'InvalidPrice' variant — the opposite grouping from the real code, which instead groups negative price together WITH the sub-cent/zero case (SubCent) and reserves the Permanent reason solely for non-finite values. The EARS text supplies no basis for either grouping, so this reason-category boundary is pure code-side surplus, and it's a boundary no A-run reconstructed correctly.

Weaker, single-run finding: A1 alone leaves negative/non-finite prices 'unhandled/pass-through' rather than adding an explicit invalid-input variant (unlike A2/A3). Since `f64 as i64` in Rust is a saturating cast, A1's sketch would silently produce `Settled(Cents(0))` for a NaN input — the opposite of the real code's explicit, loud `Err(DegradeReason::Permanent)` and never a settled/Ok value for NaN. This is more an A-internal disagreement (1 of 3 runs) than a clean directional signal, but it marks the same underspecified boundary (what to do with prices outside the 'positive number' domain) as the source of fork.

Lower-materiality implementation-level surplus: the real `price_to_cents` computes the cent value via a distinct fixed-point pipeline — scale to an integer micro-cent numerator with `SCALE = 1_000_000` via `(price_usd * 100.0 * SCALE as f64).round() as i128`, then reduce through `pt_core::round_half_to_even(numerator, SCALE)` — deliberately crossing from f64 to integer exactly once before the tie-break decision (code comment: 'the half-to-even rule — not the float's own rounding — decides the cent'). All 3 B-runs describe this pipeline and its SCALE constant identically. All 3 A-runs instead implement the tie-break as one direct call to `f64::round_ties_even(price * 100.0)` — functionally identical on the pinned test values (1.005/1.015/200.0/150.25) but a materially different, simpler technique than the real canonical `pt_core::round_half_to_even(numerator, denominator)` helper's actual signature. The EARS text names only the tie-break rule ('round_half_to_even'), not this two-stage scale/reduce implementation, so this is real but low-severity code-side surplus (an implementation-robustness choice, not an observable-behavior contract).

notes:
Scope note: several B-run observations (read_marks carry-forward semantics for Numeric+Err vs Transient, degraded-symbol absence from to_ledger_marks, TimedOut reason, quote_date stamping) describe real, consistently-pinned code behavior at the read_marks call site, but that behavior is outside the literal text of SHEET-MARK-002 (which only covers the price_usd -> Cents conversion and the positive-rounds-to-zero anomaly). Those are almost certainly the correct territory of an adjacent EARS clause (a settle-pass/degrade-classification spec) rather than drift specific to SHEET-MARK-002, so they were not counted as findings against this spec — flagging in case the parent audit wants to check whether that adjacent EARS text exists and covers them.

A-direction agreement: very high on the headline mechanism (round_half_to_even via round_ties_even, enum-shaped return distinguishing a settled value from a degraded anomaly, and — critically — treating price==0.0 as a legitimate non-anomalous value because the spec's 'positive' qualifier excludes it). Splits moderately on the un-stated edge of negative/non-finite input handling: A1 leaves it an unhandled pass-through (silently producing a bogus settled value for NaN via Rust's saturating float cast), while A2/A3 add an explicit InvalidPrice-style anomaly variant covering both negative and non-finite together. Rated medium overall given that real, substantive split.

B-direction agreement: near-total. All three reconstructions independently name the same SCALE=1_000_000 constant, the same fixed-point scale/reduce technique, the same pinned tie-break examples (1.005->100, 1.015->102), the same cents<=0 threshold covering zero/negative/rounds-to-zero as one class, and the same Permanent/SubCent reason split for non-finite vs non-positive. Rated high.
